quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Hi everyone, starting next month we will move to a four-day week for a trial period of six months. The office will be open Monday to Thursday, and everyone will keep their current salary. Customer support will still be covered on Fridays by a small rota, and anyone on the rota will receive an extra day off in return. We understand this is a big change, so we have scheduled a question-and-answer session on Wednesday at noon. Please send any concerns to Carmen in advance so that we can prepare proper answers. Thanks, Daniel
quests.question: What will happen to salaries during the trial?
options: They will depend on the Friday rota
They will stay the same
They will increase each month
They will be cut by twenty percent
quests.correctAnswer: They will stay the same
quests.hint: Ignore the schedule details and find the sentence about money.
quests.explanation: "Keep their current salary" means no change in pay. The rota only affects who works on Fridays and earns a day off.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: This week only: buy any two boxes of Sunfield cereal and get a third free, as long as all three are the same size. The offer cannot be combined with other discounts or coupons, and it is limited to six boxes per customer. Loyalty-card holders will also collect double points on all Sunfield products until Sunday. Stock is limited and the offer may end early in some stores, so shoppers are advised to visit sooner rather than later.
quests.question: Which shopper would NOT get a free third box?
options: Someone with a loyalty card who shops every week
Someone who picks a large, a medium and a small box
Someone buying six identical boxes at once
Someone shopping on Sunday before the offer ends
quests.correctAnswer: Someone who picks a large, a medium and a small box
quests.hint: Find the condition attached to the free box, then test each shopper against it.
quests.explanation: The free box needs all three to be the same size. Loyalty points are a separate extra, and six boxes is exactly the stated limit.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Students living in halls are reminded that quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. on weeknights and from midnight on weekends. Visitors are welcome until 10 p.m. but must be signed in at reception and accompanied at all times. Cooking is allowed only in the shared kitchens, and any unattended pan that sets off the alarm leads to a fine of fifty dollars. Repeated breaches can result in a formal warning and, in serious cases, loss of accommodation.
quests.question: What can happen if students repeatedly break the rules?
options: They must sign in every night
They must pay fifty dollars each time
They may be warned or lose their rooms
They are banned from the kitchens for good
quests.correctAnswer: They may be warned or lose their rooms
quests.hint: The final sentence describes the consequence of repetition, not of a single mistake.
quests.explanation: Repeated breaches lead to a warning or, in serious cases, loss of accommodation. The fifty-dollar fine is for setting off the alarm.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Online check-in opens 24 hours before departure and closes two hours before for international flights, or ninety minutes for domestic ones. Once you have checked in, you can download your boarding pass to your phone or print it at home. Passengers who need to check luggage must still drop their bags at the desk, which closes forty-five minutes before departure. Those with special assistance needs should contact the airline in advance instead of using the online system.
quests.question: What must passengers with luggage still do?
options: Take their bags to the desk before it closes
Contact the airline before travelling to the airport
Print a paper boarding pass at the airport
Check in again at the departure gate
quests.correctAnswer: Take their bags to the desk before it closes
quests.hint: A small word in the third sentence shows a step that online check-in does not replace.
quests.explanation: Checking in online does not remove the need to drop bags at the desk by the deadline. Contacting the airline is for special assistance.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Introduction to Data Analysis is a six-week course for beginners. Each week includes three short videos, a reading and a practical exercise using a free spreadsheet program. You do not need any previous experience, but you should be comfortable with basic mathematics. The course is self-paced, meaning you can watch the lessons whenever you like, although the final quiz must be completed by the end of week six to receive a certificate. Participants can join a discussion forum, where tutors answer questions on weekdays.
quests.question: What must students do to receive a certificate?
options: Complete the final quiz by the deadline
Post at least once in the discussion forum
Attend live lessons every week without exception
Pass an entry exam before joining the course
quests.correctAnswer: Complete the final quiz by the deadline
quests.hint: A word of contrast marks a rule inside an otherwise flexible course.
quests.explanation: "Although" introduces the fixed requirement: the quiz by the end of week six. The lessons themselves can be watched at any time.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Dear Mr. Novak, your bill this month is higher than usual because you used 3.2 GB of data while travelling abroad. Your plan includes roaming in Europe, but the country you visited, Turkey, is outside that area, so standard rates applied. We understand this may be a surprise. To avoid it in future, you can switch on our travel pass before you leave, which offers a daily allowance for a fixed price. We have also applied a one-time credit of ten dollars.
quests.question: Why was the bill higher than usual?
options: He exceeded his monthly call limit while away
His data plan was made more expensive by the company
Roaming charges applied outside the covered area
A travel pass was added to his account by mistake
quests.correctAnswer: Roaming charges applied outside the covered area
quests.hint: The reason follows "because" and then a "so" clause completes it.
quests.explanation: Turkey lies outside the roaming area, so standard rates were charged. The travel pass is a suggestion for the future, not something already applied.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: We are sorry to hear you wish to cancel your membership. Please note that cancellations must be made at least thirty days before your next payment date and cannot be processed at the reception desk; instead, you should complete the online form or send a letter. If you cancel within the first six months, an early-termination fee of forty dollars applies. Members who are moving more than thirty kilometres away can have the fee waived by providing proof of their new address.
quests.question: Who does not have to pay the early-termination fee?
options: Anyone who cancels at the reception desk
Members who joined a month ago
Anyone who cancels thirty days before payment
Members moving far away who show proof
quests.correctAnswer: Members moving far away who show proof
quests.hint: Look for the sentence about an exception to the fee.
quests.explanation: The fee can be waived for members moving more than thirty kilometres away with proof. Cancelling at the desk is not even accepted.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The Maple Court residents' association meets on the first Tuesday of every month at 7 p.m. in the community room. This month, the agenda includes plans for a shared garden, the state of the car park and a proposal to hold a summer street party. Anyone is welcome to attend, and people who cannot come may send comments by email to the secretary. Minutes of each meeting are posted on the notice board by the mailboxes within a week. Tea and biscuits are provided.
quests.question: How can a resident who cannot attend take part?
options: By calling the car park manager
By voting on the notice board
By sending a friend to take the minutes
By emailing comments to the secretary
quests.correctAnswer: By emailing comments to the secretary
quests.hint: Find the option offered specifically to people who are absent.
quests.explanation: Absent residents may email comments to the secretary. The notice board carries minutes afterwards, not votes.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Before an interview, research the company well enough to explain why you want to work there. Prepare two or three examples from past work that show your skills, and practise telling them briefly. On the day, arrive ten minutes early, since arriving much earlier can put pressure on the interviewer. Finally, prepare a question or two of your own; asking about training or the team shows interest and helps you judge whether the job suits you.
quests.question: Why should candidates prepare their own questions?
options: It lets candidates avoid answering hard questions
It shows interest and helps them assess the job
It gives the interviewer time to rest between answers
It is required by every employer in the country
quests.correctAnswer: It shows interest and helps them assess the job
quests.hint: The reason is given in the same sentence as the advice, after a semicolon.
quests.explanation: Questions show interest and help you judge suitability, according to the advice. Nothing suggests they are compulsory.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Due to a burst water main on Kings Road, buses on routes 8 and 14 are being diverted via Station Approach until further notice. Stops at Kings Road Market and the library will not be served; passengers should use the temporary stops on Station Approach, marked with yellow signs. Journeys will take about ten minutes longer. Route 21 is unaffected. For live updates, follow the operator's social media account or call the information line, which is open from six in the morning.
quests.question: What should passengers do to reach the library?
options: Use a temporary stop on Station Approach
Wait at Kings Road Market for a diverted bus
Call the information line for a taxi
Take route 21 along Kings Road
quests.correctAnswer: Use a temporary stop on Station Approach
quests.hint: The library is named among the stops that are not served. Look at what replaces them.
quests.explanation: The library stop is closed, and passengers are told to use the yellow-signed stops on Station Approach. Route 21 is unaffected but does not help them reach the library.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Version 4.2 of the planner app introduces shared calendars, allowing teams to see each other's availability. Because the update changes how data is stored, we recommend backing up your files first. The update will install automatically overnight on Wednesday unless you choose to postpone it in the settings, but it can only be postponed once. Users of the older version 3 will not receive this update and should upgrade manually before the end of the month, after which support will stop.
quests.question: What must users of version 3 do?
options: Wait for the automatic overnight update
Postpone the update once
Upgrade manually before support ends
Back up their files afterwards
quests.correctAnswer: Upgrade manually before support ends
quests.hint: The last sentence addresses one group of users differently from the rest.
quests.explanation: Version 3 users will not receive the update automatically, so they must upgrade themselves before support stops. The overnight install and postponing apply to newer users.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Dear parents, the Year 8 geography field trip to the coast is planned for 14 May. Pupils will study erosion and collect data, so they should bring waterproof jackets, sturdy shoes and a packed lunch. The cost of thirty-five dollars covers transport and entry to the visitor centre, and financial support is available on request. Please return the attached consent form by 30 April, indicating any medical conditions or allergies. Without a form, we cannot allow your child to take part.
quests.question: What happens if the consent form is not returned?
options: Parents must drive their child
The whole trip will be cancelled
The cost will increase
The pupil cannot join the trip
quests.correctAnswer: The pupil cannot join the trip
quests.hint: Find the sentence that begins with a word meaning "if there is no".
quests.explanation: The last sentence states that without a form the child cannot take part. Nothing suggests a price rise or cancellation.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Reservations at Olive & Thyme can be made up to thirty days in advance. For groups of eight or more, a deposit of ten dollars per person is required, refundable if you cancel at least forty-eight hours before the booking. We hold tables for fifteen minutes past the reserved time; after that, they may be given to walk-in guests. Children are welcome, though high chairs are limited, so please mention them when booking.
quests.question: When is the deposit refundable?
options: If the group arrives late for the reservation
If the booking is cancelled two days ahead
If fewer than eight people finally attend
If no high chair is available on the night
quests.correctAnswer: If the booking is cancelled two days ahead
quests.hint: Convert the hours in the condition to days before you compare the options.
quests.explanation: Forty-eight hours before the booking equals two days. Arriving late risks losing the table but does not affect the deposit rule.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Dear Ms. Chukwu, we are pleased to inform you that you have been shortlisted for the Merrin Award. The final stage is a fifteen-minute interview with a panel on 22 November, which can be held online if you live outside the region. Please prepare a short presentation about how you intend to use the funding. Successful applicants will be notified within a week, and the first payment will be made in January. We look forward to meeting you.
quests.question: What does the email ask Ms. Chukwu to prepare?
options: A written essay about her studies and future plans
A list of referees who can support her application
A short presentation on how she would use the funding
Proof of her home address in the region
quests.correctAnswer: A short presentation on how she would use the funding
quests.hint: A request in a formal email usually starts with "Please".
quests.explanation: The only preparation requested is a short presentation. The online interview option is for those living outside the region.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The Thursday Book Club is looking for new members. We meet every second Thursday at the library cafe to discuss a novel chosen by a different member each month. You do not have to finish the book; some of us read only half, and the conversation is still lively. Copies are available to borrow from the library, and the next title, chosen by Rosa, is a historical mystery set in Lisbon. Just turn up, or email Elise to join our mailing list.
quests.question: What is required to take part in a meeting?
options: Nothing special; finishing the book is optional
Borrowing a copy from Elise at the library cafe
Choosing that month's book for the whole group
Having read the whole novel before every meeting
quests.correctAnswer: Nothing special; finishing the book is optional
quests.hint: Look for a sentence that removes a possible requirement.
quests.explanation: The club says you need not finish the book, and you can simply turn up. Only one member chooses each title.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The location was excellent, only five minutes from the old town, and the staff could not have been friendlier. Our room was clean and quiet, although the bathroom was smaller than the photos suggested. Breakfast was disappointing: the choice was limited and the coffee was lukewarm. We also had to pay extra for the Wi-Fi, which was surprising for a hotel of this price. I would stay again for the position alone, but I would eat breakfast elsewhere.
quests.question: What is the reviewer's overall judgement?
options: Recommended mainly for its location and staff
Too expensive for a hotel of this kind to consider
Not recommended because of the size of the room
Excellent in every respect, from breakfast to Wi-Fi
quests.correctAnswer: Recommended mainly for its location and staff
quests.hint: Weigh the compliments against the complaints and check how the review ends.
quests.explanation: The location and staff are praised, and the writer would stay again, but the breakfast and Wi-Fi charge are criticised. The verdict is a qualified recommendation.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: If the printer does not respond, first check that it is switched on and that the cable is firmly connected. If the light is blinking orange, the paper tray may be empty or a sheet may be jammed; open the rear cover and gently remove any paper. If the problem continues, switch the printer off for one minute and then restart it. A steady red light means an internal fault, and you should contact support rather than open the casing.
quests.question: What does a steady red light indicate?
options: An empty paper tray that needs refilling
A jammed sheet of paper behind the rear cover
An internal fault that needs professional help
A loose cable between the printer and the computer
quests.correctAnswer: An internal fault that needs professional help
quests.hint: Blinking and steady lights are described differently. Keep the colours and behaviour together.
quests.explanation: A steady red light points to an internal fault and calls for support. Orange blinking relates to paper, and cables are the first thing to check.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Volunteers at the animal shelter are asked to arrive fifteen minutes before their shift and to sign in at the front desk. Please wear closed shoes and keep phones in the lockers, since animals can be startled by sudden sounds. You may walk and play with the dogs but should never open a kennel without a staff member present. If an animal seems unwell, tell the supervisor at once instead of trying to help yourself.
quests.question: Why must phones be kept in the lockers?
options: Phones are often stolen from the kennels
Sudden sounds can frighten the animals
Signals from phones disturb the kennels
They distract the supervisor during a shift
quests.correctAnswer: Sudden sounds can frighten the animals
quests.hint: A reason is often introduced by "since".
quests.explanation: Animals can be startled by sudden sounds, which is the stated reason. Nothing mentions theft or signals.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: If your flight to or from Europe is delayed by more than three hours, you may be entitled to compensation of up to six hundred euros, depending on the distance. Airlines are not required to pay if the delay was caused by extraordinary circumstances, such as severe weather or air traffic strikes. You can claim directly from the airline, or use a specialist company, which will take a percentage of any payment. Claims are usually possible for flights taken within the last three years.
quests.question: When do airlines not have to pay compensation?
options: When passengers use a specialist claims company
When the flight departs from a city outside Europe
When the delay is longer than three hours
When the delay arises from extraordinary circumstances
quests.correctAnswer: When the delay arises from extraordinary circumstances
quests.hint: The exception is introduced by a phrase meaning "is not obliged".
quests.explanation: Severe weather and strikes count as extraordinary circumstances, so no payment is owed. A delay of over three hours is the trigger for compensation, not an exemption.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Employees may work from home up to two days a week, provided their manager agrees and team meetings are not affected. Requests should be made at least a week in advance using the online form. Staff who work remotely must be available during core hours, from ten to three, and should use the company laptop, not personal computers, for security reasons. The policy will be reviewed after six months, and changes will be announced by email.
quests.question: Which requirement is linked to security?
options: Using the company laptop
Being available from ten to three
Getting the manager's approval
Asking a week in advance
quests.correctAnswer: Using the company laptop
quests.hint: Match each rule with the reason attached to it.
quests.explanation: Only the laptop rule is explained by security. The other rules concern planning, availability and approval.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Recycling bins are collected fortnightly. Please rinse containers before placing them in the bin, since food residue can spoil a whole load of paper. Plastic bags, polystyrene and greasy pizza boxes are not accepted, and bins containing them may be left uncollected with a warning sticker. Glass should be placed in the bottle banks around the city rather than in your kerbside bin. If you are unsure whether something can be recycled, check the guide on the council website.
quests.question: Why should containers be rinsed?
options: Bins are collected only twice a month
Glass must be separated first
Plastic bags are not accepted
Food residue can ruin paper for recycling
quests.correctAnswer: Food residue can ruin paper for recycling
quests.hint: The reason follows "since". Read only that clause.
quests.explanation: Food left on containers can spoil a whole load of paper. The other options are separate rules in the notice.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Sam: Are we still on for Saturday? Kim: Yes! But the cinema shows the film only at 3 and 8, and I have my sister's birthday dinner at six. Sam: Then let's do the 3 o'clock one. Kim: That leaves very little time to get to dinner. Sam: OK, what about Sunday evening instead? Kim: Perfect, Sunday at 8 works. Can you book seats? Sam: Will do. I'll message you the row numbers.
quests.question: What do they finally decide?
options: To see the 3 o'clock show on Saturday
To see the film on Sunday evening
To go to the birthday dinner together
To cancel the plan
quests.correctAnswer: To see the film on Sunday evening
quests.hint: In a chat, the final agreement is usually near the end. Follow who says "perfect".
quests.explanation: Kim accepts Sunday at 8 after rejecting the tight Saturday schedule. Saturday's 3 o'clock show was proposed but dropped.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Dear Ms. Reid, thank you for reporting the leak under your kitchen sink. A plumber is available on Tuesday between 8 and 12; unfortunately, I cannot give a more precise time. Someone over eighteen needs to be at home, and you should clear the cupboard beforehand. If the leak worsens before then, turn off the water at the stopcock, which is located behind the washing machine, and call me on my mobile. I will arrange an emergency visit.
quests.question: What should Ms. Reid do if the leak gets worse?
options: Turn off the water and phone the landlord
Clear the cupboard under the sink immediately
Wait for the plumber to arrive on Tuesday morning
Ask a neighbour over eighteen to stay at home
quests.correctAnswer: Turn off the water and phone the landlord
quests.hint: The emergency instructions are the last actions in the email, tied to "If".
quests.explanation: If it worsens, she should turn off the water at the stopcock and call. Clearing the cupboard is preparation for the planned visit.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Spring is here, and our garden centre has never looked better. This month we are introducing a new range of native plants, which need less water and attract more bees. To celebrate, we are offering a free workshop on Saturday at 10 a.m., where our experts will explain how to plan a low-maintenance border. Places are limited, so please reserve at the till. Everyone who attends will receive a ten percent discount on their next purchase.
quests.question: What is the main purpose of the newsletter?
options: To announce the closure of the garden centre
To warn customers about a shortage of bees
To promote new plants and a free workshop
To recruit new gardening staff for the summer
quests.correctAnswer: To promote new plants and a free workshop
quests.hint: Ask what the writer is trying to encourage readers to do.
quests.explanation: The text advertises native plants and invites readers to a free workshop. It contains no closure or job offer.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Dear Jordan, we are delighted to offer you a summer internship in our marketing team, beginning on 1 July and lasting ten weeks. The position is paid at eighteen dollars an hour for thirty hours a week. You will work with a mentor and contribute to a real campaign; at the end, you will present your work to senior staff. Please confirm your acceptance by replying before Friday, and we will send the contract and details of your first day.
quests.question: What will Jordan do at the end of the internship?
options: Train the next group of interns
Begin a new campaign
Present the work to senior staff
Sign a permanent contract
quests.correctAnswer: Present the work to senior staff
quests.hint: Look for a phrase that marks the final stage of the placement.
quests.explanation: "At the end, you will present your work" describes the closing task. The contract mentioned is for the internship itself.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: The night train from Vienna sounded romantic, but the reality was cramped. My compartment held six bunks, and by midnight the air was stuffy. Yet at dawn, when I pulled up the blind, I saw mist over a valley and a village with a church on a hill. That view alone repaid the trouble. My advice to anyone considering the trip: book a lower bunk, bring earplugs and keep the window blind open at sunrise.
quests.question: What is the writer's attitude to the journey?
options: Indifferent about the whole experience
Completely delighted with every part of it
Entirely negative from beginning to end
Mixed, but ultimately positive
quests.correctAnswer: Mixed, but ultimately positive
quests.hint: Look at how the mood changes after "Yet".
quests.explanation: The cramped night is balanced by the beautiful dawn, and the writer still recommends the trip with tips. That is a mixed but positive view.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Electricity supply to parts of Oakridge will be interrupted on Thursday between 9 a.m. and 3 p.m. while engineers replace an underground cable. Affected customers have been sent letters, but if you live near the school or on Fairview Road, you can expect a short outage even if you did not receive one. Please switch off sensitive equipment, such as computers, before the work begins. If you rely on medical devices that need power, call the priority line so that we can make special arrangements.
quests.question: Who should call the priority line?
options: Residents of Fairview Road
Anyone with a computer
Customers who did not receive a letter
People who rely on powered medical devices
quests.correctAnswer: People who rely on powered medical devices
quests.hint: The last sentence names the group for whom the line exists.
quests.explanation: The line is for those who need power for medical devices. Fairview Road residents may have an outage but are not asked to call.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: This year, the charity's income rose by eight percent, largely because of a successful spring appeal and a growing number of monthly donors. Spending on programmes increased more slowly, at four percent, as the board decided to build a reserve fund. Administrative costs fell to nine percent of income, the lowest level in a decade. Looking ahead, the trustees plan to open a second training centre, but warn that this depends on continued donations and on securing a suitable building.
quests.question: Why did spending on programmes grow more slowly than income?
options: Fewer donors gave money than in the previous year
The board chose to build up a reserve
The spring appeal failed to raise its target
Administrative costs increased faster than income
quests.correctAnswer: The board chose to build up a reserve
quests.hint: Compare the two growth rates, then find the reason given for the gap.
quests.explanation: Income rose by 8 percent while programme spending rose by 4, and the text says the board created a reserve. Administrative costs actually fell.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: To claim for stolen belongings, first report the theft to the local police and obtain a written report. Next, contact us within thirty days, either online or by phone, and give the report number. You will need to provide receipts or bank statements as proof of ownership for items worth more than two hundred dollars. Once we have everything, decisions are normally made within ten working days. Please note that claims for items left unattended in a public place may be refused.
quests.question: What must be done before contacting the insurer?
options: Report the loss online
Wait for a decision
Collect receipts for every item
Get a written police report
quests.correctAnswer: Get a written police report
quests.hint: Order words such as "first" and "next" decide the answer here.
quests.explanation: The police report comes first and is needed for the report number. Receipts are required only for expensive items and are provided after contact.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: This course examines how cities are planned and how planning decisions affect everyday life. The first half concentrates on history, from medieval streets to modern suburbs, while the second half looks at current challenges such as housing costs, transport and climate. Assessment is by a group project, worth forty percent, and a final essay, worth sixty. Students are encouraged to visit different neighbourhoods and to bring their observations to seminars, which count for participation but not for the mark.
quests.question: What contributes most to the final mark?
options: Neighbourhood visits
The final essay
The group project
Seminar participation
quests.correctAnswer: The final essay
quests.hint: Compare the two percentages, then check the exceptions in the last sentence.
quests.explanation: The essay is worth sixty percent against forty for the project. Seminars and visits do not count towards the mark.
